newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end down, properties lead fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end down, properties lead fall.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended down, but off its lows on Tuesday with property counters leading the fall.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index bounced off an intraday low of 2,004.82 to end at 2,014.78, down 15.43 points on the day. Dealers said the weak market sentiment was exacerbated by thin volumes.
"Property counters were very weak in the afternoon," said one broker. The SES property index ended down 8.98 points at 691.46 led by falls in DBS Land, Singapore Land and City Developments.
"The market is down on talk that recent launches, even at good property sites like Balmoral Road, had not been well-received," said another dealer.
Topping the actives list were Keppel Land warrants with over 13 million shares traded. They closed four cents up at S$1.32.
Audio products-related company Datapulse was also active with more than 11 million shares changing hands, inclusive of 10 million crossed at S$0.72. It closed at S$0.74.
HongKong Land also closed lower after recent sharp gains. It ended at US$2.78, down 21 cents on volume of 8.3 million units.
